founder.name: Yannick Benewende Rapadamnaba
founder.shortBio: Self-taught tech enthusiast, born in Gagnoa, of Ivorian-Burkinabè origin. Five years of learning driven by one conviction: master technology to build what's needed — and African tech independence. Outio is the first cornerstone.
founder.longBio:
Self-taught over five years with a singular conviction: knowledge and mastery come first. Build what's needed, build to last — don't ride waves. Outio is the first tangible outcome and the starting point of a broader ambition.

His thesis: we're living through a global tech tipping point. AI is crossing from software into the physical world. Africa risks being left behind — this void must be filled. Open source changes the game: create and innovate locally, build technology transfer partnerships with open-minded partners — particularly in Asia —, and protect data through local servers.

Born in Gagnoa, western Côte d'Ivoire, of Ivorian-Burkinabè origin, based in Abidjan. This coast ↔ Sahel bridge is a strategic asset, not a biographical detail.
founder.quote: The need is immense. We have the minds, the brains, and with the right resources, the power to drive real change. Africa must have its own applications and its own technological independence. I believe in it — and I'm going to make it happen.

thesis.title: AI value has shifted from access to assembly
thesis.body: Raw models have become a commodity — open source, free, interchangeable. The edge is no longer the model, but the ability to assemble the right tools into a system that delivers concrete results, and to distribute it where no one else does. OpenBaara is that assembly and distribution layer, for markets global players don't serve.
thesis.quote: The AI divide won't be between those who know how to use it, but between those who own it and those who depend on it.
